author: orchestrator
content: Developer rejected plan v1: Plan critic returned revise on both rounds; one high-severity issue stands. BLOCKING: plan requirements 1 and 3 (accepts only a demonstrably interrupted IMPLEMENTING task; fail closed when the interruption cannot be established) have no acceptance criterion that exercises refusal. AC-1 covers only the eligible path and AC-3 covers only the lock override, so recover could be implemented as an unconditional status setter - accepting a task in any state, one with a terminating event, or one already carrying CLAUDE_FIX_STARTED - and all 16 verify commands would still pass. That is exactly the hand-edit defect the verb exists to remove. Also unresolved: nothing asserts the interrupted work on disk survives recovery, so a recovery that reset files would pass; AC-9 does not settle that the rounds-exhausted blocking critique specifically is persisted, nor its round/plan-version identity; AC-16 rests on a baseline test count the implementer itself picks, so a low literal satisfies it; AC-12 needs a hand-rolled ci.yml reader under stdlib-only and must fail rather than skip when the file is missing or unparsable; all 16 criteria are unittest tests the implementer authors and none drives orchestrator.py as a subprocess through real CLI dispatch; CLAUDE.md is not declared, so its verb list and its IMPLEMENTING-has-one-exit narrative will contradict the code; and _support.py is declared while its fixture work could be written inline, risking a declared-but-unchanged validation failure. requirement.md has been extended with criteria 14-18 and three new constraints covering all of the above - read it before replanning. KEEP from v1: the file set is right, including .ai/hooks/session_start.py, .ai/hooks/stop_guard.py and .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py, and AC-14 and AC-15 correctly single-home the blackboard and make the guard read the authoritative approved plan.

author: orchestrator
content: Developer rejected plan v2: Plan critic passed v2, but five substantive non-blocking issues stand and two of them are not polish. (1) AC-3 weakens a fail-closed guarantee in translation: the requirement says a recovered task cannot reach VALIDATED without validation having run, while AC-3 only asserts recovery emits no validation or completion event. Not emitting an event during recover does not settle that the route afterwards still requires validation. (2) The plan calls the persisted critique artifact orchestrator-owned evidence, but PROTECTED_EVIDENCE_PATTERNS in .ai/hooks/pre_tool_use.py lists only state.json, events.jsonl, baseline.json, test-results.json, validation.md and review-findings.json. As planned this ships a new evidence file a worker can write its own version of, which contradicts the rule that no plan can authorise a worker to write its own verdict. Both pre_tool_use.py and CLAUDE.md are already declared, so this needs no change to the file set. (3) Requirement criterion 8 is half covered: nothing asserts worker and acceptance subprocess launching falls back to the orchestrator checkout when state.worktree is null, and TASK-008 own state.json has worktree null, so this is the path this very task runs on. (4) AC-3 bundles lock refusal, override attribution and no-manufactured-completion into one implementer-authored test method; unbundle them. (5) AC-18 never states where the critique artifact lives or how it is named, so a developer told to read it at the gate cannot find it and a reviewer cannot tell a stale round from the current one. Additionally, F2 residual case must be written into the plan risks: structural ownership leaves a concurrent task with no recorded worktree editing shared source still producing blocking violations in task A. That narrowing follows from decision 2 and is accepted, but it must be accepted knowingly. requirement.md now carries criteria 19-23 covering all of the above. KEEP v2 wholesale otherwise: the 14-file set is right, and AC-14/15/16 refusal paths, AC-17 byte preservation, AC-19 real CLI subprocess dispatch, AC-20 CLAUDE.md verb-contract parsing and AC-12 fail-not-skip are all correct and must be retained.

author: orchestrator
content: Developer rejected plan v3: Plan v3 passed the critic, but four of its five remaining issues are closed by developer decision rather than accepted. (1) AC-3 carries two claims and its command settles one: the statement says lock refusal happens without using a PID liveness probe as authorization, but test_existing_lock_refuses_without_override only tests refusal in general, so an implementation that probes os.kill(pid,0) and proceeds when the pid looks dead would satisfy the command while violating decision 4. Add an explicit dead-PID test proving PID liveness cannot authorize recovery; pid data may be advisory detail in the event only. (2) Constraint 3 keeps recovery metadata out of state.json because task-state.schema.json sets additionalProperties false, but no criterion enforces it - validate the post-recovery state.json against that schema and assert it passes. (3) The declared file list can strand the implementer. Rooting subprocesses at the recorded worktree most plausibly changes worker_env, and test_preflight.py (which calls orch.worker_env for a task with no state or worktree), test_worktree_pr.py, test_validation_profile.py and test_review_package.py all exercise that or cwd/merge-base behaviour while undeclared. AC-16 requires the whole suite to pass, so a behaviour change breaking any of them leaves the implementer unable to fix it (undeclared write, denied at the tool boundary) and unable to leave it (criterion fails). Re-evaluate and correct the file list: preferably design the change to be backward compatible and state in the plan why each module is unaffected, otherwise declare only those that genuinely must change, remembering a declared file left byte-identical fails as declared-but-unchanged. Do not leave a path where AC-16 fails while the implementer is forbidden to fix the failing test. (5) Make hook resolution authoritative and testable. .claude/settings.json registers hooks as cwd-relative commands, so once worker cwd is the recorded worktree the scripts that execute are that worktree copies, not the orchestrator checkout copies. Decide explicitly which copy is authoritative, state it in the plan, and add a criterion proving the intended copy ran - AC-27 and AC-28 currently pass either way, so neither settles it. Issue 4 (the ADR for worktree-rooted execution with single-homed evidence) may remain a documented non-blocking risk; write it only if it falls out naturally, do not expand scope. requirement.md now carries criteria 24-27 covering all of the above. KEEP v3 otherwise in full: objective, the 15 requirements, all 28 existing criteria, constraints 1-18 including constraint 17 about extending fd35909 rather than re-deriving it, and risks 4, 7 and 10.

author: claude
content: A test process running inside an orchestrated worker session inherits ORCHESTRATOR_REPO_ROOT / TASK_DIR / WORKER_ROOT / CONSTITUTION, and the hooks now read those exports by design. So an existing test that launches a hook with a fixture cwd and an inherited environment resolves the real TASK-008 evidence instead of its fixture's: test_plan_authorization.py, test_hardening.py's run_hook and test_context_bus.py's HookBehaviourTests produce 14 extra failures that way, e.g. test_undeclared_script_is_denied passes ALLOW because plan-v4 really does declare .ai/scripts/orchestrator.py. Not a guard defect and not a validation problem: the orchestrator runs validation from its own environment, and with those variables cleared full discovery is 722 tests OK. Every test added in this task builds its subprocess environment explicitly with ORCHESTRATOR_* stripped. Fix any future occurrence by scrubbing the environment in the test, never by weakening exported-root resolution in the hooks.
evidence: py -3 -m unittest (inside worker session): 15 failures, 1 error
env -u ORCHESTRATOR_* py -3 -m unittest: 722 tests OK

author: claude
content: BASELINE_EXCLUDE_PREFIXES drops '.worktrees/' and '.ai/tasks/' from the manifest, so a change under another task's conventional worktree never reaches any task's delta at all. Structural 'foreign' classification therefore bites only where another open task's recorded worktree is somewhere the manifest still enumerates (an unconventional or absolute recorded path). AC-7's fixture records the second task at sandboxes/TASK-998 for that reason; a fixture in .worktrees/ would have produced an empty delta and asserted nothing.

author: claude
content: The two failures ctx-005 recorded were fixture defects in the new test_run_driver.py, not defects in the recover verb: test_recovery_event_records_reason_and_developer never called _interrupted(), so load_state raised FileNotFoundError for TASK-999; and test_recovered_task_requires_validation_before_validated wrote its .ai/validation.json after write_baseline(), making the profile task-produced and undeclared, so validation failed on diff-scope and the task read FAILED instead of VALIDATED. Both fixed in the fixture with no assertion changed. Fixture ordering matters generally: write_baseline() must come after everything the fixture means as pre-existing.

author: orchestrator
content: Independently reproduced the high review finding before routing. Confirmed by reading the code, not by trusting the reviewer: task_dir() returns the relative Path(.ai)/tasks/<id> (orchestrator.py:189); run_worker sets cwd=execution_root(task_id) (orchestrator.py:574); the implement prompt interpolates that relative requirement_file and plan_file (orchestrator.py:2274-2296) and the fix prompt does the same; and .gitignore deliberately tracks .ai/tasks/, so a worktree carries a committed and possibly stale copy of the plan. For any task with a recorded worktree the worker therefore resolves the plan against the worktree copy rather than the approved bytes, which defeats the hash-bound approval that pre_tool_use.approved_plan() was hardened to protect. This did not affect the TASK-008 run itself: TASK-008 state.worktree is null, so execution_root falls back to the orchestrator checkout and both roots are the same directory. The defect is latent, not observed in this run. Also reproduced the environment-inheritance issue the fix worker flagged, and it is wider than reported: running the suite with ORCHESTRATOR_REPO_ROOT/TASK_DIR/WORKER_ROOT/TASK_ID inherited yields 16 failures, not 14, across test_hardening (4), test_context_bus (4) and test_plan_authorization (8). test_plan_authorization was not named in implementation.md. The reviewers found the same root cause independently as a medium correctness and a low security finding. Validation itself is unaffected because the orchestrator validates from its own clean environment, which is how the 722-test run and 32/32 criteria were recorded.

author: claude
content: Fix pass 3 closed the planner half of the high finding and gave prompt/planner path resolution its first coverage. codex_argv now emits str(authoritative_path(plan_file)) for --output-last-message, which covers run_codex_planning and run_codex_replan at one place; both stopped shadowing the module's repo_root() with a local. What is deliberately NOT absolute: the plan path returned and recorded in events.jsonl and state.json stays repo-relative, so evidence still compares across machines - only the string handed to the subprocess is absolute. test_worker_launch.WorktreeEvidencePathTests (5 tests) asserts implement prompt, fix prompt, planning output and replan output all name checkout-rooted evidence with cwd verified to be the recorded worktree; assertEvidenceIsCheckoutRooted compares occurrence counts of the bare filename against the absolute path, so a second relative mention anywhere in a prompt fails it. Verified as non-decorative: with orch.authoritative_path patched to identity and evidence_dir to task_dir - the pre-fix behaviour - all four of those tests fail. Suite is 729 tests OK with ORCHESTRATOR_* cleared. One thing left undecided rather than fixed: the planner's --cd is still the orchestrator checkout while run_worker's cwd is the recorded worktree, so a planner run for a task with a worktree analyses the checkout. Not a regression and no criterion covers it, but --cd also selects the --output-schema copy, so changing it is a decision someone should take deliberately.

author: claude
content: run_recover treated lock_holder() as the flag meaning 'a lock existed', and lock_holder returns None for a zero-byte or unreadable .lock. task_lock creates the file with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and writes the pid line afterwards, so a process killed between the two leaves exactly that lock - the interruption recover exists for. With an empty lock and an override supplied the old code wrote no RECOVERY_LOCK_OVERRIDDEN event, recorded lock_overridden=False, and never unlinked the file, so route-failure then refused with 'locked by another invocation (unknown)' and the task was stranded again by the verb meant to unstrand it. Existence is now the flag; the holder stays advisory and is recorded as 'unknown' when the file says nothing. The unlink is no longer suppressed with 'Removing ...' printed in advance: removal is attempted first, success prints 'Removed', an OSError is reported with what it means for the next verb, and the event carries lock_removed so the trail records what happened rather than what was intended. Covered by test_run_driver.RecoverLockSafetyTests.test_an_empty_lock_is_still_a_lock and test_a_lock_that_cannot_be_removed_is_reported_not_swallowed. This was a medium reviewer finding, not the routed high one; it was fixed because it lives in this task's own new code in an already-declared file and its effect is the exact stranding recover exists to remove.

author: orchestrator
content: Validation now has fresh recorded evidence (test-results.json 18:34) and the result is 31 of 32 criteria passed, 0 unverified, 0 unproven, 1 failed. The one failure is AC-16, returncode 124, "timed out after 300s". This is NOT a defect in the code under test. The suite itself passes: the tests check recorded 729 tests OK in 232.9s, and an independent foreground run of the same discovery command passed 729 tests OK in 227.5s. The cause is structural. AC-16 verify re-runs full unittest discovery as an acceptance command, and acceptance commands are capped by ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_S = 300 at orchestrator.py:23, while the tests check runs under the larger VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_S. A suite that legitimately takes ~230s standalone exceeds 300s when run again as the 16th of 32 criteria on a loaded host. Plan-v4 predicted this in its own risk list ("running the entire suite and the four explicit compatibility modules in separate criteria duplicates work and may approach validation time limits on slower Windows hosts") and the performance reviewer filed it as a low finding against test_task_baseline.py. It has now moved from predicted to actual. The decision this needs is not obvious and should not be taken by the worker alone. ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_S is a repo-wide constant governing every task's acceptance commands, so raising it is a workflow-wide behaviour change, even though orchestrator.py is a declared file and raising it would not weaken AC-16 (the criterion still requires the full non-empty suite to pass; only the runner's patience changes). What must NOT be done to make this green: narrowing AC-16, deleting the duplicate tests check, editing the undeclared .ai/validation.json, or trimming tests. Each would make the number pass by measuring less, and C12 forbids weakening the suite.

author: claude
content: AC-16's timeout was suite wall time, and the suite was already near the cap before this task. Measured on one host with ORCHESTRATOR_* cleared: 107.3s/729 tests at the failing state, and 92.2s/659 tests at fd35909 (measured by cloning the worktree to a temp dir and checking out the baseline commit - same host, same interpreter). Per-class profiling attributes the +15s to this task's new test classes, not to slower orchestrator code: pre-existing test_task_baseline classes cost 27.5s vs 29.0s at baseline, pre-existing test_hardening classes 2.9s vs 2.8s. 67.5s of 70.5s in the two slowest modules is subprocess time, dominated by per-test git repository construction at ~0.4s per test method on Windows (init + 2 config + add + commit + checkout). Fix: build the starting repo once per task id into a temp template and shutil.copytree it per test (0.400s -> 0.051s), which took test_task_baseline from 35.4s to 21.4s with no assertion changed; and batch test_repo_hygiene's per-tracked-file git check-ignore into one --stdin call, 5.5s -> 0.8s. Equivalence of the copied fixture was checked, not assumed: right branch, empty status and diff, single base commit, same tracked set. AC-16's own command now runs 729 tests OK in 85s - faster than the pre-task baseline while carrying 70 more tests. ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_S is deliberately untouched per ctx-015; the residual exposure is host load, since the validating host measured 232.9s where this session measures 107s for the same bytes (~2.2x), which at 85s puts AC-16 near 190s against the 300s cap. TRAP for anyone batching git via subprocess on Windows: text=True rewrites the input separator to CRLF, git takes the CR as part of the path and quotes it, so every check-ignore match silently inverts - it produced 8 inverted assertions here. Write bytes with -z. Also noted and left alone: four live 'claude --print --agent failure-classifier' calls happen during the suite (1.7s here) from route_failure tests that do not set ORCHESTRATOR_DISABLE_CLASSIFIER=1, the one part of suite duration this repo does not control.
evidence: AC-16 verify command: discovered 729, Ran 729 tests, OK, 85s
git status/diff/log/ls-files probe of a copied fixture repo
compute_task_delta: 14 declared files modified, created and deleted empty

author: claude
content: Correction to ctx-016's single 85s figure, because the failure being fixed is a timeout and one draw is not the distribution. Four post-fix full runs on this host, all green: 82.6s, 84.0s, 98.8s, 150.8s. Pre-fix on the same host: 107.3s and 107.5s. The 150.8s run is the same bytes as the 84.0s one, minutes apart, so run-to-run spread on one host is larger than the ~20-25s the fix saves. Consequence for anyone reading AC-16's next result: this pass lowers the probability of the timeout, it does not make the criterion structurally safe. ~50s of the remaining suite is test_review_package (42.9s) plus test_validation_profile (6.7s), both undeclared and byte-identical by plan constraint, so the worker-side lever is nearly exhausted. If AC-16 times out again the remaining options are the repo-wide ACCEPTANCE_TIMEOUT_S raise (which does not weaken the criterion - the full non-empty suite must still pass) or removing AC-16's duplication of the tests check, and both are developer decisions per ctx-015.
evidence: four post-fix full-discovery runs: 82.6s, 84.0s, 98.8s, 150.8s, all 729 tests OK
